q-31412.solution:
If we let $u=-x$, then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,-\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {§n§}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {§n§}^{u}\cdot (-1)\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int {§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}+C \\  & =-\frac{{§n§}^{-x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-31413.solution:
If we let $u=5x$, then 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {§n§}^{5x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {§n§}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\int {§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}+C \\  & =\frac{{§n§}^{5x}}{5\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-31417.solution:
If we let $u=\frac{x}{3},$ then,

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3\text{d}u.
$$

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {§n§}^{x/3}\,\text{d}x & =\int {§n§}^{u}\cdot 3\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\int {§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}+C \\  & =\frac{3\cdot {§n§}^{x/3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-30973.solution:
If we let $u=6x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6\,⟹\,\frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $6$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of  $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{§n§}^{6x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{6}{§n§}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{0}^{6}{§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}){|}_{0}^{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}(§upper§-§lower§) \\  & =\frac{§delta§}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§} \\  & =\frac{§halfdelta§}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}\end{aligned}
$$

q-349625.solution:
If we let $u=7-2x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2\,⟹\,-\frac{1}{2}\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $5$ | $3$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{§n§}^{7-2x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{5}^{3}{§n§}^{u}(-\frac{1}{2})\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{5}^{3}{§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}){|}_{5}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}({§n§}^{3}-{§n§}^{5}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}(§upper§-§lower§) \\  & =§final_op_spaced§\end{aligned}
$$

q-349626.solution:
If we let $u=5-x,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,-\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $4$ | $2$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}3\cdot {§n§}^{5-x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{4}^{2}3\cdot {§n§}^{u}(-1)\text{d}u \\  & =-3{\int }_{4}^{2}{§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-3(\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}){|}_{4}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}({§n§}^{2}-{§n§}^{4}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}(§upper§-§lower§) \\  & =§final_op_spaced§\end{aligned}
$$

q-349631.solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,-\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}2\cdot {§n§}^{1-x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{0}2\cdot {§n§}^{u}(-1)\text{d}u \\  & =-2{\int }_{1}^{0}{§n§}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-2(\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}){|}_{1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}({§n§}^{0}-{§n§}^{1}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}(§upper§-§lower§) \\  & =§final_op_spaced§\end{aligned}

q-349646.solution:
If we let $u=x-1,$ then

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $-1$ | $1$ |

Then, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{§n§}^{x-1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{§n§}^{u}\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{§n§}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}\,{|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}({§n§}^{1}-{§n§}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡§n§}(§upper§-§lower§) \\  & =§final_op_spaced§\end{aligned}
$$

q-349648.solution:

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.

Computing our limits of integration, we get the following:

| --- | --- | --- |

$$
